standard_prerequisites: the duality formula Hom_{D(O_X)}(K, M) = H^0(X, K^vee tensor^L M) for K perfect with dual K^vee (Cohomology on Sites, Lemma sites-cohomology-lemma-dual-perfect-complex)

perfectness of an object of D_QCoh checked etale locally (Cohomology on Sites, Lemma sites-cohomology-lemma-perfect-independent-representative)
Rj_* commutes with direct sums for quasi-compact separated morphisms j (lemma-quasi-coherence-pushforward-direct-sums of the same chapter) and the adjunction between restriction and Rj_*

comparison of D_QCoh on the small etale site with the scheme case (lemma-derived-quasi-coherent-small-etale-site and lemma-descend-perfect of the same chapter) and the scheme proposition perfect-proposition-compact-is-perfect of Derived Categories of Schemes
core_obligations: Prove that an object of D_QCoh(O_X) is compact if and only if it is perfect, for X quasi-compact and quasi-separated over the base scheme S
proof_roadmap: For K perfect: Hom(K, M) = H^0(X, K^vee tensor^L M) functorially in M; tensoring with the dual K^vee and global H^0 both commute with direct sums on D_QCoh, so Hom(K, -) preserves direct sums, which is compactness of K.

Conversely, perfectness is etale-local, so it suffices to show K|_U is perfect for every affine etale U -> X; the morphism j : U -> X is quasi-compact and separated, hence Rj_* commutes with direct sums, and the adjunction between restriction and Rj_* shows K|_U is compact in D_QCoh(O_U).
For affine U the comparison lemma and descend-perfect reduce the claim to the scheme proposition of Derived Categories of Schemes, closing the argument.
difficulty_reason: H3: a two-direction argument whose forward direction is a duality computation with direct sums and whose converse is a localization reduction to the known scheme case.
